article_title: Specialized AI and neurosurgeons in niche expertise: a proof-of-concept in neuromodulation with vagus nerve stimulation.
citation: Barrit Sami, Ranuzzi Giovanni, Fetzer Steffen, Al Barajraji Mejdeddine, Hadwe Salim El, Zanello Marc, Ortler Martin, O'Flaherty Julieta, Massager Nicolas, Madsen Joseph R., Dibué Maxine, Carron Romain. (2025). Specialized AI and neurosurgeons in niche expertise: a proof-of-concept in neuromodulation with vagus nerve stimulation. Acta Neurochirurgica. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00701-025-06610-8
title: VNS masterclass MCQ assessment: 14 items with 67 binary propositions scored from -1 to +1 per question
description: The assessment instrument was an MCQ in which "The MCQ consisted of 14 items (Supplemental Material 3) containing 67 assertive propositions", each requiring a binary true/false judgment. Scoring assigned or deducted a fraction of 1/n per proposition, with total scores ranging from -1 (all incorrect) to +1 (all correct) per question, so a score of zero represented performance equivalent to random chance. It was designed by three neurosurgeons and one technical expert to test practical clinical knowledge for safe and effective VNS implementation.
requirements: Questions must test practical clinical knowledge required for safe and effective VNS implementation rather than theoretical or research-oriented concepts, as the faculty designed them
constraints: The authors state that MCQs do not fully capture the complexity of real-world clinical settings
target_learners: board-certified neurosurgeons already performing VNS procedures
target_learning_goals: VNS clinical management, surgical anatomy, procedural steps, and technical aspects
examples: All 36 course attendees completed the assessment after a 2-day masterclass including theoretical instruction, practical workshops, and surgical cadaver-based training

(2025). Specialized AI and neurosurgeons in niche expertise: a proof-of-concept in neuromodulation with vagus nerve stimulation. Acta Neurochirurgica. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00701-025-06610-8

article_title: Evaluation of ChatGPT and Microsoft Bing AI Chat Performances on Physics Exams of Vietnamese National High School Graduation Examination
citation: Xuan-Quy Dao, Ngoc-Bich Le, Xuan-Dung Phan, Bac-Bien Ngo, The-Duy Vo. (2023). Evaluation of ChatGPT and Microsoft Bing AI Chat Performances on Physics Exams of Vietnamese National High School Graduation Examination. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.04538
title: VNHSGE physics evaluation subset: 2000 multiple-choice questions in 50 test sets across four difficulty levels
description: The VNHSGE dataset is a benchmark compiled from real Vietnamese National High School Graduation Examination papers from 2019 to 2023, covering nine subjects. Its physics subset contains "2000 multiple-choice questions divided into 50 sets of test questions" spanning topics such as mechanical oscillations, electromagnetic waves, and light refraction. Questions are classified into four levels from knowledge to high application, and the dataset is released in JSON and Word formats for LLM evaluation. The study used a five-exam, 200-question evaluation subset from it.
requirements: Questions, formulas, and figures must be converted to text format for compatibility with language models such as BERT and GPT
constraints: The evaluation subset comprised five illustrative exams (200 multiple-choice questions) for 2019–2023, not the full 2000-question set
target_learning_goals: high school physics proficiency across knowledge, comprehension, application, and high application levels
examples: The authors evaluated ChatGPT (Feb 13 version) and BingChat (April 15 version) on five illustrative exams of 200 multiple-choice questions offered by the Vietnamese Ministry of Education and Training for 2019–2023
key_sources: Xuan-Quy Dao, Ngoc-Bich Le, Xuan-Dung Phan, Bac-Bien Ngo, The-Duy Vo. (2023). Evaluation of ChatGPT and Microsoft Bing AI Chat Performances on Physics Exams of Vietnamese National High School Graduation Examination. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.04538

article_title: ChatGPT is Good but Bing Chat is Better for Vietnamese Students
citation: Xuan-Quy Dao and Ngoc-Bich Le. (2023). ChatGPT is Good but Bing Chat is Better for Vietnamese Students. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.08272
title: VNHSGE dataset for evaluating LLMs on Vietnamese high school examinations
description: The VNHSGE dataset is a benchmark derived from the Vietnamese National High School Graduation Examination and comparable examinations, built by the authors to assess LLM performance in Vietnamese education. It "encompasses nine distinct subjects" and "comprises a total of 300 literary essays and 19,000 multiple-choice questions pertaining to various subjects." The present study uses an evaluation set drawn from it: 30 literature essay questions and 1700 multiple-choice questions from the 2019–2023 exams. It supports multitask evaluation including question answering, text generation, reading comprehension, and visual question answering.
requirements: Questions are drawn from the VNHSGE examination and comparable examinations, spanning nine subjects
constraints: The evaluation set used in this study covers exam years 2019 to 2023 only
target_learners: Vietnamese high school students preparing for the VNHSGE examination
target_learning_goals: Assessing LLM capability across nine high school subjects including mathematics, literature, English, physics, chemistry, biology, history, geography, and civic education
examples: This study's evaluation set: 30 essay questions for literature and 1700 multiple-choice questions from 2019–2023 exams
key_sources: Xuan-Quy Dao and Ngoc-Bich Le. (2023). ChatGPT is Good but Bing Chat is Better for Vietnamese Students. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.08272
